sources.name: RiverBrain Heller Bar Boat Ramp access record
observations: Names Heller Bar Boat Ramp as a Snake River take-out, gives the exact shared route coordinate 46.08601938,-116.98350549, and describes a concrete ramp, toilets, and parking.
The WDFW water-access-site point is about 103 feet away, consistent with a facility/site point distinct from the specific ramp endpoint.
sources.limits: RiverBrain publishes an access-point coordinate but does not identify it as a surveyed wet toe; the hydrology audit still places the point away from its mapped flowline and water polygon.

sources.name: Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife Heller Bar access page
observations: Confirms a year-round public WDFW-managed Heller Bar access site with one concrete boat ramp and one hand launch.
WDFW also lists parking and restrooms at the location.
sources.limits: The web page confirms the facility and ramp, but does not publish a precise ramp-toe coordinate.

sources.name: WDFW official Water Access Sites GIS feature layer
observations: The WDFW water-access-site feature is named Heller Bar and its published point is 46.0857522742,-116.9833745081, approximately 103 feet from the RiverBrain ramp point.
This is the agency's access-site point; its small offset from the RiverBrain ramp point does not support replacing the route endpoint with a separate site centroid.
sources.limits: The ArcGIS feature is a site point, not a delineated ramp or shoreline geometry.

sources.name: American Whitewater Heller Bar Snake River access record
observations: Confirms Heller Bar is a road-accessible Snake River take-out used by floaters from the Lower Salmon, Snake, and Grande Ronde rivers.
Its access point is 46.08349,-116.98261, about 950 feet from the shared route point, so it does not establish a replacement for the ramp coordinate used by RiverBrain.
sources.limits: The separate American Whitewater point is a broad access marker and is materially displaced from the exact ramp endpoint documented by RiverBrain.

sources.name: WDFW wildlife-program maintenance report
observations: WDFW staff report that the underwater gravel bar in front of the Heller Bar ramp becomes exposed at lower summer flows, corroborating a variable ramp-to-water interface.
sources.limits: The report discusses seasonal conditions but does not provide a coordinate.

sources.name: Bureau of Land Management Lower Salmon recreation-season page
observations: Describes the Lower Salmon reach to its Snake River confluence followed by an additional 20-mile trip along the Snake to the Heller Bar take-out, supporting Heller Bar as the terminal access for the lower-Salmon route after the confluence.
sources.limits: Confirms the route connection and Heller Bar take-out, but does not publish a precise ramp coordinate.

decision: Retain the RiverBrain ramp coordinate because it matches the exact named endpoint and is corroborated by the managing agency's concrete-ramp record; classify it as an authoritative access-site anchor and keep its mapped-water offset reviewable.
